pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Medium-sized irregular polygons with high-angularity serrated edges. Patches on the flank exhibit a stellate geometry with sharp pixel gradients transitioning to light corridors. Patch size decreases and becomes more curvilinear toward the posterior hindquarters.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous network of light-cream pathways forming a complex topological graph. Junction nodes are predominantly tri-valent. Pathway thickness is relatively uniform across the mid-flank with slight tapering at the convergence of three or more patches.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: High-frequency, low-amplitude dark serrated contour visible along the upper neck and shoulder transition. The silhouette is comprised of short, dense vertical pixel clusters against the background.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: Localized textural disruption and reddish-brown hyper-pigmentation visible at the base of the neck/shoulder area, indicating a focal skin anomaly.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A distinct, dark reddish-brown lesion or wound is visible on the lower left cervical-thoracic junction, characterized by an irregular perimeter and loss of standard pelage pattern in that specific coordinate.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of a symbiotic avian organism (Oxpecker) clinging to the lower neck region, causing a localized occlusion and textural anomaly on the pelage.
